title: I'm not a developer but I spent the last weeks making a dark-fantasy dice roguelite with AI — here's Osselets
author: Matiesyx
selftext:
I'm not a developer but I directed everything (rules, story, balance, art direction) and AI wrote the code and generated the images and music.  
  
Osselets is a dark-fantasy dice roguelite. Your die is your deck: each face is an item, you roll, reroll, chain combos, and every monster breaks the rules in its own way.

The story: the gods gambled the world away on dice, and someone cheated. You play Ysolde, going down 40+ floors where her mother never came back from, holding the last honest die. 

It's still in development and I'm updating it almost every day. It's free, in your browser, on phone or computer: [https://osselets.pages.dev/?de=reddit-aigamedev](https://osselets.pages.dev/?de=reddit-aigamedev)

If you give it a few runs, I'd love your feedback: what's confusing, what's too hard or too easy, where you stopped. Every comment helps.

comments.author: TriggerHappyPermaBan
comments.body: One thing I noticed when using ai-agents to design screens and hud, they cannot differentiate game design from Saas and modern web design. You have the main gothic visuals, but everything around it is Saas-like/web-dashboard design, which break the feeling of fantasy.

replies.author: Matiesyx
replies.body:
I agree. I think we're at the very beginning of coding with AI. It's already much easier than it was 6 months ago, and models will keep improving in the coming months.  
It's nice, though, to bring our ideas to life without any coding skills.  
Happy to receive feedback on the game btw :)
